summary: This week brought momentum on multiple fronts: disclosure advocates are preparing to demand transparency measures before Congress on Tuesday, MITRE has agreed to comply with a lawmaker's request for UAP records dating back to 1930, and several newly declassified flight incident reports entered the archives. The White House's "Alien.gov" website generated confusion and debate when it turned out to focus on immigration rather than UAPs, though the simultaneous release of Pentagon UFO files and Steven Spielberg's "Disclosure Day" film kept public attention on the genuine government documents. Meanwhile, key figures like Lue Elizondo continued to emphasize that transparency efforts are irreversible, even as skeptics argued the disclosure process faces institutional roadblocks. A whistleblower also alleged the CIA had explored consumer DNA databases to investigate potential extraterrestrial connections, adding another layer to the week's revelations about what agencies have investigated behind closed doors.
